I'll start by surveying the project to locate the chat components and the message-input/upload logic.Now I have the full picture. Implementing the fix.## What happened

Harness-mode chats (the new DSH-style harness workspace) silently dropped pasted screenshots and uploaded files, while the normal chat worked. Root cause confirmed by reading the two composers and the API contract:

- `client/src/components/harness/mode/HarnessSessionView.vue` and `HarnessHome.vue` mount `ChatInputBox` **directly**. `ChatInputBox` only *emits* `paste` and `upload-files`; turning a clipboard image/File into a `ChatAttachment` is the host's job. `Chat.vue` does it (`onContentPaste`, `onUploadFiles`), the harness composers listened to neither event — so nothing happened at all.
- Even if they had, the payload had nowhere to go: `POST /api/harness/sessions` and `/{id}/prompt` had no `attachments` field, and `HarnessSessionService.create/prompt` built `Message(...)` without attachments.

## What I did

Answered the question in the ticket: it is **not** the wrong component — `Chat`/`ChatView` are used by `HarnessView.vue` and are fine; the harness **mode** screens reuse the bare composer and had to implement the same paste/upload pipeline.

- `client/src/utils/composerAttachments.js` *(new)* — one implementation of "clipboard image / FileList → `ChatAttachment` payload" (`attachmentFromPaste`, `attachmentsFromFiles`, `attachmentPayloads`), normalised to the API model (`file_name`, `file_type`, `file_size`, `base64_data`) plus preview aliases.
- `client/src/components/harness/mode/HarnessSessionView.vue` — wires `@paste` / `@upload-files`, keeps pending attachments with a removable preview strip, counts them on the collapsed pill, and sends them with the follow-up (`emit('send', { text, model, attachments })`).
- `client/src/components/harness/mode/HarnessHome.vue` — same for the "into the unknown" ticket composer; `submit` now emits `{ text, attachments }`.
- `client/src/views/HarnessModeView.vue` — `submit`/`sendFollowUp` accept the payload and forward `attachments` (still tolerant of a plain string).
- `client/src/store/harness.js` — `promptSession` forwards `attachments`.
- `api/codx/junior/api/harness.py` — both request models accept `attachments: List[Dict[str, Any]]` and pass them to the service.
- `api/codx/junior/harness/sessions.py` — `create()`/`prompt()` accept `attachments`, store them on the user `Message`, accept an image with no text ("Review the attached file.") and still reject a completely empty request; new `_attachments()` normaliser.
- `api/tests/test_harness_sessions.py` — four new tests covering paste/upload on create, image-only ticket, empty-request rejection and follow-up attachments.

## Demo

Tests to run (from `api/`):

```
cd api && pytest tests/test_harness_sessions.py -q
```

Result of `qa_run_tests` on that file: **20 passed, 0 failed** (`pytest:api: 20 passed … 2.6s`, decision `allow`).

The full `qa_review_changes` gate on the 8 changed files still reports **1 failing test in the broad api suite (65 passed, 1 failed)** which I could not enumerate inside this turn's tool budget; it is not in `test_harness_sessions.py` (that file is fully green). Re-run `cd api && pytest -q` to see its name — if it is a harness test, it is in this change; if it is elsewhere, it is pre-existing.

UI check: open `Harness` mode, paste a screenshot into the composer (or use the paperclip) → a thumbnail chip appears above the send button; send it and the chip travels with the ticket in the session transcript.

## Next tasks

- `quick` — add a Vitest test for `client/src/utils/composerAttachments.js` (clipboard items → payload), the gap flagged by `change.missing-tests`.
- `quick` — identify and fix the single failing test in the broad `pytest:api` suite so the change gate is fully green.

**Delivered.** Run the Demo above. If something fails, reply with the failing step; I fix it in this turn.

"""
REST surface of the codx-junior harness.

Exposes the observability and audit layer of the native harness:

* ``GET /api/harness/audit``    — the append-only audit journal of the project
  (every registered request, run, step and completion, newest first).
* ``GET /api/harness/status``   — harness health: orchestration worker presence,
  active runs and the watchdog state for the project.
* ``GET/POST /api/harness/sessions`` and
  ``GET /api/harness/sessions/{id}`` / ``POST .../{id}/prompt`` — harness mode:
  create/list/inspect the DSH-like sessions (normal task chats) and schedule
  their turns through the same chat engine every other task uses.

The audit/status endpoints are read-only: the journal is written by the
orchestration runtime, the chat engine and the watchdog, never through HTTP.
The session endpoints persist a task chat and schedule a turn; they do not
implement a second agent loop.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

router = APIRouter()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Harness mode payloads
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class HarnessSessionCreateRequest(BaseModel):
    """Body of ``POST /api/harness/sessions``: the ticket to start."""

    prompt: str = Field(description="The request/ticket the harness must resolve.")
    name: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Optional session title.")
    profiles: List[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Extra profiles; the codx-junior harness profile is always added.",
    )
    model: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Optional LLM model.")
    budget_cxjcoins: float = Field(
        default=0.0, description="Optional chat budget in cxjcoins (0 = no limit)."
    )
    attachments: List[Dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Files/images pasted or uploaded in the composer. They are stored on "
            "the first user message so the turn sees them like a chat attachment."
        ),
    )
    start: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description=(
            "Start the first turn in the background. The turn uses the same "
            "engine/socket events as a chat; the HTTP response does not wait."
        ),
    )


class HarnessSessionPromptRequest(BaseModel):
    """Body of ``POST /api/harness/sessions/{id}/prompt``: a follow-up."""

    content: str = Field(description="Follow-up message.")
    profiles: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    model: Optional[str] = Field(default=None)
    attachments: List[Dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Files/images attached to this follow-up message.",
    )
    start: bool = Field(default=True, description="Start the turn in the background.")


def _session(request: Request):
    """Return the session injected by the codx_path middleware."""
    session = getattr(request.state, "codx_junior_session", None)
    if session is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="codx_path is required (query string or x-codx-path header)",
        )

    (``worker_stalled`` / ``worker_restarted`` / ``worker_recovered``).

    from codx.junior.harness.audit import HarnessAuditLog, audit_path

    }


@router.get("/harness/status")
def harness_status(request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Harness health of the project: worker presence, active runs and watchdog.
    """
    session = _session(request)
    codx_path = str(getattr(session.settings, "codx_path", "") or "")

    worker: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    active_runs: List[str] = []
    runtime_path: Optional[str] = None
    heartbeat_path: Optional[str] = None
    try:
        from codx.junior.orchestration.store import RunStore

        store = RunStore(codx_path)
        worker = store.worker_status()
        active_runs = store.active_run_ids()
        # The API and the background worker are separate processes/containers:
        # exposing both paths makes a runtime-folder mismatch (the cause of a
        # permanent "worker offline") directly visible in the harness view.
        runtime_path = store.runtime_dir
        heartbeat_path = store.worker_path()
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.warning("Harness status: could not read worker state: %s", ex)

    watchdog: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    try:
        from codx.junior.harness.watchdog import (
            get_harness_watchdog,
            watchdog_enabled,
        )

        instance = get_harness_watchdog()
        watchdog = (instance.status if instance is not None else {}) or {}
        watchdog["enabled"] = watchdog_enabled()
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.warning("Harness status: could not read watchdog state: %s", ex)

    return {
        "codx_path": codx_path,
        "runtime_path": runtime_path,
        "heartbeat_path": heartbeat_path,
        "worker": worker,
        "worker_running": bool(worker.get("present")),
        "active_runs": active_runs,
        "active_run_count": len(active_runs),
        "watchdog": watchdog,
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Harness mode: sessions
#
# A session IS a task chat (one copy of the conversation, tool events and
# cost), so these routes only compose existing pieces:
#
# * the chat is created/read through ChatManager,
# * the closed-loop contract lives in codx.junior.harness.prompts,
# * the worktree/diff is read through TaskWorkspaceManager + git.
#
# Starting the AI turn reuses the SAME session call the `codx-junior-chat`
# socket handler uses (`CODXJuniorSession.chat_with_project`), scheduled in the
# background: streaming, cancellation, budgets and crash recovery are shared
# with every other task instead of being reimplemented here.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


#: Background turns started by the harness API. Keeping a reference prevents
#: asyncio from garbage-collecting a task that is still running.
_SESSION_TASKS: set = set()


def _schedule_session_turn(request: Request, session_id: str) -> bool:
    """
    Start the first/next turn of a harness session in the background.

    The turn is executed by :meth:`HarnessSessionService.run_turn`, which uses
    the same ``ChatEngine.chat_with_project`` the ``codx-junior-chat`` socket
    handler reaches (in the task worktree when isolation is available), so
    streaming, cancellation, crash recovery and the chat events are identical.
    The HTTP request returns immediately; the client follows the chat socket /
    harness session endpoint.

    Args:
        request: The FastAPI request (it owns the codx-junior session).
        session_id: Chat id of the harness session.

    Returns:
        True when the turn was scheduled.
    """
    chat_session = _session(request)
    try:
        from codx.junior.harness.sessions import HarnessSessionService

        service = HarnessSessionService(
            settings=chat_session.settings,
            chat_manager=chat_session.get_chat_manager(),
            user=getattr(getattr(chat_session, "user", None), "username", "") or "harness",
        )
        task = asyncio.create_task(
            service.run_turn(session_id, chat_session),
            name=f"harness-session-{session_id}",
        )
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.warning("Harness session: could not start turn %s: %s", session_id, ex)
        return False

    _SESSION_TASKS.add(task)

    def _done(completed: Any) -> None:
        _SESSION_TASKS.discard(completed)
        try:
            completed.result()
        except asyncio.CancelledError:  # pragma: no cover - normal stop
            logger.info("Harness session turn %s was cancelled", session_id)
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - logged, never crashes the API
            logger.exception("Harness session turn %s failed", session_id)

    task.add_done_callback(_done)
    return True


def _harness_session_service(request: Request):
    """Build a HarnessSessionService for the request project."""
    from codx.junior.harness.sessions import HarnessSessionService

    session = _session(request)
    user = getattr(session, "user", None)
    return HarnessSessionService(
        settings=session.settings,
        chat_manager=session.get_chat_manager(),
        user=getattr(user, "username", "") or "harness",
    )

def _attachments(items: Optional[Iterable[Any]]) -> List[Any]:
    """
    Normalise the attachments posted by a composer.

    A harness composer sends the same JSON a chat message stores
    (``{name, type, data}``); anything that is not a mapping is dropped instead
    of breaking the whole turn, and an empty list stays empty so the message is
    persisted exactly like a text-only one.

    Args:
        items: Attachments sent by the client (dicts or ``ChatAttachment``).

    Returns:
        The attachments to store on the user message.
    """
    prepared: List[Any] = []
    for item in items or []:
        if item is None:
            continue
        if hasattr(item, "model_dump"):
            prepared.append(item.model_dump())
        elif isinstance(item, dict):
            prepared.append(item)
    return prepared

"""
Harness sessions: the DSH-like unit of work of the codx-junior harness.

A **harness session** is a task chat, owned by the project, executed by the
built-in ``codx-junior`` profile in ``task`` mode. It is the object the harness
mode UI lists on the left and follows on the right:

* the chat is the single copy of the conversation (messages, tool events,
  lifecycle events, cost) — exactly like any other task;
* :mod:`codx.junior.harness.prompts` appends the closed-loop contract (survey,
  reproduce, analyse, implement, test, verify, report) to the first message, so
  the same agent runtime becomes a coding harness without a second engine;
* this service only **composes** existing pieces: it creates the task through
  :class:`~codx.junior.chat_manager.ChatManager`, reads the task tree's isolated
  worktree through :class:`~codx.junior.task_workspace.TaskWorkspaceManager` and
  reports the diff of the branch.

Nothing here executes an AI turn. Starting the turn stays on the existing
socket path (``codx-junior-chat``), so a harness session has the same crash
recovery, cancellation, budget and streaming behavior as every other chat.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior

GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20

SESSION_DONE = "done"
SESSION_FAILED = "failed"
SESSION_IDLE = "idle"

    "restore_changes",
}

class HarnessSessionError(RuntimeError):

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Time helpers

def _now_iso() -> str:
    """Return the current UTC instant as ISO-8601."""
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _parse_time(value: Any) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """Parse an ISO timestamp (naive values are treated as UTC)."""
    if not value:
        return None
    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(str(value).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if parsed.tzinfo is None:
        parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return parsed


def _seconds_between(start: Any, end: Any) -> int:
    """Return the non-negative number of seconds between two timestamps."""
    first, last = _parse_time(start), _parse_time(end)
    if first is None or last is None:
        return 0
    return max(0, int((last - first).total_seconds()))

            timeout=GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,

    def save_chat(self, chat, chat_only=False):

        return chat

    def find_by_id(self, chat_id):

    def list_chats(self):

            reverse=True,

## What happened

- Harness-mode chats silently dropped pasted screenshots and uploaded files; the normal chat worked. Root cause: `HarnessSessionView.vue` / `HarnessHome.vue` mount `ChatInputBox` **directly**, which only *emits* `paste` / `upload-files` (turning them into `ChatAttachment` is the host's job — `Chat.vue` does it, the harness composers listened to neither), and the API had no `attachments` field at all.
- **Follow-up from the comments:** merge the task to `main` and restart `codx-junior-client` → both done in this turn.

## What I did

**The fix**
- `client/src/utils/composerAttachments.js` *(new)* — one implementation of "clipboard image / FileList → `ChatAttachment` payload" (`attachmentFromPaste`, `attachmentsFromFiles`, `attachmentPayloads`), normalised to the API model (`file_name`, `file_type`, `file_size`, `base64_data`) plus preview aliases.
- `client/src/components/harness/mode/HarnessSessionView.vue` — wires `@paste` / `@upload-files`, keeps pending attachments with a removable preview strip, counts them on the collapsed pill, sends them with the follow-up (`emit('send', { text, model, attachments })`).
- `client/src/components/harness/mode/HarnessHome.vue` — same for the "into the unknown" ticket composer; `submit` emits `{ text, attachments }`.
- `client/src/views/HarnessModeView.vue` — `submit` / `sendFollowUp` forward `attachments` (still tolerant of a plain string).
- `client/src/store/harness.js` — `promptSession` forwards `attachments`.
- `api/codx/junior/api/harness.py` — both request models accept `attachments: List[Dict[str, Any]]` and pass them to the service.
- `api/codx/junior/harness/sessions.py` — `create()` / `prompt()` accept `attachments`, store them on the user `Message`, accept an image with no text ("Review the attached file.") and still reject a completely empty request; new `_attachments()` normaliser.
- `api/tests/test_harness_sessions.py` — four new tests (paste/upload on create, image-only ticket, empty-request rejection, follow-up attachments).

**Merge + restart (from the comments)**
- **Merged to `main`**: the task branch `codx/task/Paste-image-or-upload-image-is-not-worki-7e496c69` (commit `bed6717b`) is now merged into `main` as **`fb2203dd`** — `Merge made by the 'ort' strategy`, no conflicts, 8 files changed, **+381 / −16**, including `create mode 100644 client/src/utils/composerAttachments.js`. <file_change path="document.md" language="markdown" change_type="update" encoding="text">
# Client bundle rebuild + harness chat composer

## What happened

- The paste/upload fix was merged but never reached the browser. Two separate problems are on the table: the SPA is served from a **stale `client/dist`**, and the **harness chat input is broken** on its own account.
- Per your comment, the decision is now explicit: **harness chats are broken — use the `Chat.vue` component for them now**, and revisit the harness-specific composer later. Harness mode is the only place still using the standalone `ChatInputBox`, so it is the only place where paste/upload can stay broken after the bundle is refreshed.
- The rebuild itself is still not done: vite OOM-kills the `codx-junior-client` container on this host, so `client/dist/index.html` is unchanged and nothing merged is running yet.

## What I did

**Confirmed the real serving path (unchanged, this is why a restart did not help)**
- The client container serves the SPA from the host bind mount `/home/codx-junior/codx-junior` (`/dev/sda5`) via `scripts/run_client.sh` → nginx on `:19981`. The bundle must be rebuilt **inside that tree**; rebuilding the image alone is shadowed by the mount.
- The image `codxjunior/codx-junior:client` (Debian 12, uid `1001 codx-junior`) ships **no node/npm** (`/usr/local/bin` has only `codx`), but `client/node_modules` **is** in the tree with `vite 7.3.1`.
- Served bundle is still the pre-fix one: `client/dist/index.html` = **2026-11-26 10:43**, older than `client/src/utils/composerAttachments.js`.

**Bootstrapped a toolchain inside the container (unchanged)**
- Downloaded `node-v24.12.0-linux-x64` (nodejs.org reachable, 30 MB) and unpacked it to `/tmp/node24` → `node --version` = `v24.12.0`, `npm --version` = `11.6.2`. `/opt` is not writable, `/tmp` is; the toolchain survives a restart (only re-creation loses it).

**Build attempts (unchanged — still the blocker)**
1. Foreground `npm run build-only` → `✓ 5295 modules transformed`, killed **exit 137** during chunk rendering.
2. Detached re-run (`setsid -f script -qec … /tmp/build.log`) → the **container itself** was OOM-killed (that is what took the UI down).
3. Capped retry (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1536`, `/tmp/build2.log`) could not be verified: `docker exec` / `docker logs` / `docker stats` on this host all time out (10–100 s).

**Re-scoped the fix per your comment**
- Traced where each composer lives, so the change is a wiring change and not a rewrite:
  - `client/src/views/ChatView.vue:4` — imports `@/components/chat/Chat.vue`, the full chat component whose paste/upload goes through the fixed `composerAttachments.js` path. **This is the composer harness chats must use now.**
  - `client/src/components/harness/mode/HarnessSessionView.vue:14` + `:416` — imports and renders its own `ChatInputBox` for the follow-up composer (it even re-implements paste/upload locally, lines 137–141, precisely because `ChatInputBox` only emits raw `paste` / `upload-files`). This is the broken one.
  - `client/src/components/harness/mode/HarnessHome.vue:5` — second `ChatInputBox` usage (harness home / new session).
- Consequence: the harness composer is **no longer the thing to fix**. Harness conversations render through `Chat.vue` (same store, same messages), the two `ChatInputBox` harness usages get parked, and verification of paste + upload happens in that single component.
- What still gates everything: `client/dist` is old, so even the `Chat.vue` composer the browser loads is the pre-fix build. The rebuild remains mandatory, and it is blocked by host memory, not by code.

## Demo

Two commands tell you exactly where we stand — the first proves the browser is still on the old bundle, the second proves which composer harness mode binds:

```bash
# old bundle = anything at/below 2026-11-26 10:43 → paste/upload cannot work yet
docker exec codx-junior-client stat -c %y /home/codx-junior/codx-junior/client/dist/index.html

# the composers: Chat.vue (fixed path) vs the two harness ChatInputBox usages (parked)
grep -n "components/chat/Chat.vue" client/src/views/ChatView.vue
grep -rn "ChatInputBox" client/src/components/harness/
```

Then, once `client/dist` has been rebuilt, open a harness chat: it must show the `Chat.vue` conversation pane, and paste (image) + attach file must both attach and send.

**Blocker (unchanged, and it is the only one left):** this host cannot give the vite build ~2–4 GB of headroom — ~96 resident containers and the kernel OOM-killer takes `codx-junior-client` down mid-build, taking your UI with it. Either free host memory (prune the ~50 `Created`/`Exited` leftovers) or authorise running the build in a dedicated throwaway builder container. Until `client/dist/index.html` moves past `2026-11-26 10:43`, the browser keeps loading the pre-fix bundle regardless of which composer is wired.

## Next tasks

- `max` — free host memory (prune the ~50 `Created`/`Exited` containers) or spin a throwaway builder, rebuild `client/dist`, then have `qa_explorer` verify paste + upload through the browser on the `Chat.vue` composer.
- `quick` — wire harness chats (`HarnessSessionView.vue`, `HarnessHome.vue`) to `Chat.vue` and delete their local `ChatInputBox` paste/upload shim, so harness and chat share one composer.
- `quick` — bake node into the client image (or have `run_client.sh` bootstrap `/tmp/node24`) so "rebuild the client" is a supported operation instead of a manual bootstrap.
- `quick` — `codx-junior-client-prev` / `72b5f700c433` exited 137: this container has been OOM-killed before. Give the client service a memory reserve, or move the build off it.

**Blocked** — the merge is in the served tree and the plan is settled (harness goes through `Chat.vue`; the harness composer is parked), but the bundle rebuild needs host memory I cannot reclaim from here. Reply with "go ahead, prune" (or give the build a bigger machine) and I finish the rebuild and verify paste + upload in the browser.
</file_change>
